summary: Move every desktop keyboard shortcut into one registry in src/shared/shortcuts.ts (id, label, group, scope, bindings written with Mod), read it from the global resolver, the app menu, the Cmd+W intercept, the command palette hints, the Settings list and the components that own their keys, and stop Ctrl chords from firing app commands on macOS. Adds pure override and clash-detection functions for a later editing UI.

reactNativeIos.reason: The React Native client has no keyboard shortcuts: nothing under apps/mobile/src handles onKeyPress or hardware key events, and touch is its only input. The registry is in src/shared, so it can be imported there if one is ever added.

nativeAndroid.reason: The native Android client handles no hardware key events (no KeyEvent, onKeyEvent or isCtrlPressed under apps/android/app/src/main), so there is no shortcut to register.

sharedBackendApi.reason: No IPC channel, wire frame or backend handler changes. The registry lives in src/shared because both the Electron main process (menu accelerators, Cmd+W intercept) and the renderer read it, but it is not part of any transport contract.

storageDataMigration.reason: Nothing is stored yet. applyShortcutOverrides takes a command id to bindings map for the later Settings editor, which will choose the settings key; malformed overrides are ignored so a bad stored value cannot break the defaults.

updateRelease.reason: Desktop code change only. No package identity, signing, deep link, update channel or native module change.

automated: tests/unit/global-keybindings-terminal.test.ts mounts a real xterm in jsdom with the App's window capture listener and asserts Ctrl+K/J/B/L/T reach the PTY with no app action on macOS; it fails 6 of 7 against the previous resolver.
tests/unit/shortcuts.test.ts covers registry validity, per-OS matching and formatting, Electron accelerators, overrides and clash detection.
The existing tests/unit/global-keybindings.test.ts cases pass unchanged against the registry-backed resolver (the Ctrl case now runs as the non-macOS platform).
notExercised: The Windows and Linux builds were not run; Ctrl-as-Mod there is covered by unit tests only.
The Electron menu accelerators and the Cmd+W before-input-event path were not driven by a test; they read the same registry values the unit tests pin.
